title: Preference leaderboard: position swaps, Elo, contested prompts
scenario: Pairwise rater judgements (some from a legacy UI that swapped positions) are cleaned, deduped per rater/prompt/pair, and turned into win rates, Elo (K=32) and a list of contested prompts. Test 2 is the leaderboard and disagreement list.

verified.why_correct: The exponent (rb - ra) looks reversed, but when ra > rb it is negative, 10**negative < 1 and the result is above 0.5, so the stronger player is favoured, as the Elo formula in the README says.

bugs.title: Comparison rater ids not lower-cased
bugs.symptom: Both files fail. Test 1: used is 18 instead of 22; atlas-7b shows 11 games / 7 wins; Elo becomes borealis 966.8, cirrus-2 987.4, drift-xl 1009.7. Test 2: leaderboard swaps borealis and cirrus-2, and contested is ['p03', 'p04'] (p06 and p10 missing).
bugs.why: The registry ids are lower-cased but comparison rater ids are only trimmed, so every 'R07' row fails the `rater not in qualified` check and is silently dropped.
bugs.unblocks: used, win rates and Elo in Test 1, and p06/p10 in contested. Exposes B2.
hints: used is 18, not 22. Which rows went missing, and what do they have in common?
Compare how rater ids are cleaned in load_raters and read_comparisons.
probes: Why is r07 in the qualified set even though raters.json has a trailing space?
Why were these rows dropped silently instead of raising an error?

bugs.title: swapped = "false" treated as swapped
bugs.symptom: Only visible after B1 is fixed. Test 1: used stays 22, but atlas-7b shows 9 wins (win_rate 0.731) and Elo shifts (borealis 956.5, cirrus-2 984.6, drift-xl 1004.0). Test 2: leaderboard swaps borealis and cirrus-2, and contested is ['p03', 'p04', 'p08', 'p10'] (p08 instead of p06).
bugs.why: bool() of any non-empty string is True, so R07's rows marked 'false'/'False' get their winner flipped. Blank cells still give False, so only the rater who fills the column is affected.
bugs.unblocks: Test 1 win rates and Elo, and p06 in contested.
hints: Look at R07's p06 and p08 rows. Who should have won each?
Look at how the swapped column is interpreted.
probes: Why was this invisible until rater ids were fixed?
Why did R07's 'true'/'TRUE' rows come out right even with this change?

bugs.title: groupby over unsorted comparisons
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_contested_prompts only: ['p04', 'p10'] instead of ['p03', 'p04', 'p06', 'p10']. Test 1 and the leaderboard pass.
bugs.why: itertools.groupby only groups adjacent items. The comparisons are in time order, so p03's and p06's judgements are split by other rows into separate one-item groups and their disagreement is never seen.
hints: p04 and p10 are found but p03 isn't. Where are p03's rows in the kept list?
Look at how contested() groups comparisons.
probes: Why did p04 and p10 still come out right?
What would a dict/defaultdict version look like, and why doesn't it need sorting?

context_qa.a: load_raters returns the set of qualified rater ids; read_comparisons filters and resolves rows to Comparison objects; latest_only dedupes and returns them in (created_at, row) order; then elo, win_rates and contested are computed from that list, and the leaderboard is sorted from the Elo dict.

context_qa.q: What does a Comparison look like?
context_qa.a: prompt_id, rater, pair (the two model ids as a sorted tuple), winner (a model id, or None for a tie), created_at (datetime) and row (the CSV line number, header = 1).

context_qa.q: How does read_comparisons decide which rows to keep?
context_qa.a: It cleans the rater id and the winner letter, and skips the row if the rater is not in the qualified set or the letter isn't a/b/tie. It then reads the swapped flag, flips a<->b if set, and maps the letter to model_a/model_b (tie -> None).

context_qa.q: How does latest_only break ties between duplicate judgements?
context_qa.a: It keys by (rater, prompt_id, pair) and replaces the stored comparison when (created_at, row) is greater, so later times win and, at equal times, the later CSV row wins.

context_qa.q: How is Elo updated per comparison?
context_qa.a: With a, b = c.pair, score_a is 1, 0 or 0.5, delta = K * (score_a - expected(Ra, Rb)), then Ra += delta and Rb -= delta. Ratings start at 1000 via a defaultdict and are rounded to 1 decimal at the end.
It uses itertools.groupby with the key (prompt_id, pair) and adds the prompt id when a group's set of winners has more than one value (None counts as a value).
